terminal.description: The page runs in the Browser panel and reloads every time you save. The shell is here if you want to look around the files.

tasks.title: Show the picture of the studio
tasks.description:
Show the drawing of the studio front just under the main heading in `index.html`. The file is `studio.svg`, in the `pictures` folder next to `index.html`.

The check looks for an image of `studio.svg` and makes sure its address leads to the real file.
nextSteps: Read "The image element" in the lesson.
Add an image element right after the main heading.
Point its source at the file, starting from the folder `index.html` is in.
Save, look for the drawing in the Browser panel, and press Check.
hints: An image has no closing tag. The file goes in an attribute.
The address is relative, like a link to another page, and the file is one folder down.
Write an `img` whose `src` is the folder name, a slash and the file name.

videos.title: Images in HTML in three minutes

tasks.title: Describe the pictures
tasks.description:
Give both pictures on the page the alt text they need.

- The studio picture shows something a visitor should know about. Describe what it shows in a few words.
- The wavy divider is only decoration. Mark it so a screen reader skips it.

The check reads the alt text of each picture. A description is at least three words, is not a file name, and does not start with "picture of".
nextSteps: Look at the studio drawing and say out loud what is in it.
Write that as the studio picture's alt text.
Give the divider the alt value for decoration, save and press Check.
hints: Imagine telling someone on the phone what the studio drawing shows, in one short sentence.
Decoration still gets an alt attribute. Leaving it out is not the same as leaving it empty.
The studio picture gets `alt="..."` with your sentence in it. The divider gets `alt=""`, two quotes with nothing between them.

tasks.title: Give the studio picture its size
tasks.description:
Tell the browser how big the studio picture is before it loads, so the text under it does not jump. Its real size is written on the first line of `pictures/studio.svg`.

The check reads the width and height attributes of the studio picture and compares them with the file.
nextSteps: Read "Width and height" in the lesson.
Open `pictures/studio.svg` from the files list and find its width and height on the first line.
Add the two size attributes to the studio picture.
hints: The size goes in two attributes on the image element, one for each direction.
The numbers come from the svg file. Copy them as plain numbers, without `px`.
Add `width="640"` and `height="400"` to the studio picture.

tasks.title: Caption the mug of the month
tasks.description:
In the shop section, the line `Mug of the month: ...` should sit under a picture of the mug.

- show `pictures/mug.svg` with alt text that says what the mug looks like
- group the picture and the line in a figure, with the line as its caption

The check looks for the mug picture inside a figure, the caption inside the same figure, and the mug's alt text.
nextSteps: Read "Figures and captions" in the lesson.
Wrap the line about the mug of the month in a figure.
Add the mug picture inside the figure, then turn the line into its caption.
Save, look at the shop section in the Browser panel, and press Check.
hints: Two new elements work together here: one around the whole group, one around the caption.
The paragraph around the caption line is replaced by the caption element. The picture sits next to it, inside the group.
Use `<figure>` around an `img` of the mug and a `<figcaption>` that holds the line.
